rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, pretrain_steps=0, n_iter=25, grad_clip=1.0, outer_wall_s=1400, per_scene_s=None, batch_size=1, lr=0.0003, optimizer=adam, unet_c=16, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=iter-19 SIX-BOX. (1) PRIOR: iter-18 hr=0.0, warm_start OFF at matched n_iter=50 gave rmse=0.00659 (WORST) -- vs iter-6's warm-started 0.00628 at the SAME n_iter, confirming the warm-start provides a materially better init (from-scratch 50 steps is under-fit). Iters 1-18 all hr=0. NOTE: verified the solver HARDCODES torch.optim.Adam (the `optimizer` cfg key is a no-op), so I do NOT test optimizer as it would be a fake lever. (2) FAILURE MODE: plain-UNet N2I at the over-smoothed FBP-consistent plateau; no edge-preserving structural guard (bilateral sibling range kernel hr~0.21). (3) ONE KNOB: relative to iter-6 best reference (warm_start=True, lr=3e-4, c=16), n_iter 50 -> 25 (extreme early-stop, below all prior 50/100/200/400). Extends the inner-step sweep to its minimal end: freeze the recon almost AT the warm-start init. (4) HYPOTHESIS: with only 25 per-image steps the recon stays closest to the warm-started init; if the warm-start init is the least-over-smoothed point and per-image steps only push toward the smooth mean, 25 steps should give the LOWEST rmse of the n_iter sweep. If it dips toward baseline, minimal-step early-stop is the lever. Per the ceiling, expect hr=0 -- the warm-start init is itself over-smoothed, so freezing near it just yields a blurry recon (rmse ~0.0063). (5) BUDGET: 25 steps/scene very fast; pretrain ep=3 + 200*25-step fits + figure ~= 8 min << 30-min wall. (6) Loop continues; iter-20 (FINAL) self-dispatched. Reserved final lever: per_scene_s explicit to guarantee full deep-fit completion, OR a confirmatory replicate of the best config.
